chunks: What Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a traveler who arrives in a land. He said: If he resolves within himself to stay ten days, then let him perform in full. But if he says, “Today I will leave,” or, “Tomorrow I will leave,” while not knowing, then let him shorten between that time and one month. Then if a month passes, let him perform in full. And he does not perform in full in less than ten days except in Makkah and al-Madīnah; and if he stays in Makkah and al-Madīnah for five days, then let him perform in full.

key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: al-Madīnah, where a special ruling is mentioned
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler whose salat ruling is under discussion
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Makkah, where a special ruling is mentioned
key_terms.شَهْرٍ: one month, the limit of continued uncertainty before full prayer applies
key_terms.عَشْرًا: ten days, the threshold for performing salat in full
key_terms.فَلْيُتِمَّ: let him perform the prayer in full
key_terms.يُقِيمَ: to intend to stay or reside

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who does not know how long he will stay in a place?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for a traveler who enters a place without knowing how long he will remain. If he intends to stay ten days, he performs salat in full; if he remains uncertain day by day, he continues to shorten until one month passes, after which he performs in full. It also states a special ruling for Makkah and al-Madīnah, where completing salat applies after a stay of five days.
